text.title: Multi-Region Failover Pattern Pack — Procedure
text.summary: Nine steps from two agreed numbers to a drilled pack: get RPO/RTO per tier from the business owner, collect replication lag, backfill and dependency facts, choose the pattern whose achievable numbers fit and whose capacity and quotas are real, write the DNS, database and object-store mechanics, list dependencies with bypasses, write failback, run the live drill and record measurements, then decide and label verified or unverified.

step.name: agree-rpo-rto-per-tier
step.input: Workload tier list; the business owner for the tier.
step.action: Record `workload.name`, `tier`, `business_owner`, and the agreed `rpo_minutes` and `rto_minutes` in `inputs[]`, plus `primary_region` and `secondary_region`. An unassigned workload takes the strictest tier's numbers.
step.decision-gate: "Near zero", "as fast as possible" or "same as today" stops the procedure here (r-rpo-rto-numeric-per-tier).

step.name: collect-replication-facts
step.input: Database replication metrics for the last 30 days; object-store replication configuration and metrics.
step.action: Fill `database.engine`, `replication`, `p99_lag_seconds_30d`; fill `object_store.replication_enabled`, `versioning`, `backlog_metric`, `replication_time_alert`, `existing_objects_backfilled` and the `backfill_job` (on Amazon S3, the Batch Replication job id).
step.decision-gate: Asynchronous replication with p99 lag above `rpo_minutes` × 60 s means either the RPO goes up or replication goes synchronous and is re-costed (r-database-replication-mode-and-promotion, r-object-store-replication-verified).

step.name: list-region-scoped-dependencies
step.input: Everything the failover script and the secondary region touch: IdP, secrets manager, CI/CD, DNS provider, certificates, payment and email providers, cloud control-plane endpoints.
step.action: Fill `dependencies[]` with `kind` and `reachable_from_secondary`; for each unreachable one write the `bypass` (replicated copy, break-glass path, manual step).
step.output: `dependencies[]` with at least the IdP, DNS provider and CI/CD.
step.decision-gate: An unreachable dependency with no bypass invalidates any pattern claim (r-region-scoped-dependencies-listed).

step.name: choose-pattern-and-capacity
step.input: Required RPO/RTO; cost per pattern; secondary capacity and regional service quotas.
step.action: Choose one of backup-and-restore, pilot-light, warm-standby, active-passive-hot-standby, active-active. Record `achievable_rpo_minutes` / `achievable_rto_minutes`, `secondary_capacity.mode`, `percent_of_primary`, `scale_up_minutes` (for scale-up), and `quotas_verified` after requesting quotas in the secondary region for full production load.
step.decision-gate: Achievable RTO above required, or scale-up time above RTO, or quotas not requested: choose the next pattern up and re-cost (r-pattern-chosen-from-rpo-rto-and-cost, fm-07).

step.name: write-dns-mechanics
step.input: DNS provider configuration; client inventory (mobile SDKs, server-side connection pools).
step.action: Set `dns.mechanism`; for dns-failover set `ttl_seconds` (60 or less on failover records), `health_check` endpoint / interval / failure threshold; list `ttl_ignoring_clients[]` with a `fallback` each. `observed_propagation_seconds` is filled from the drill in step 8.
step.decision-gate: A TTL above 60 s on the failover record is rejected (r-dns-failover-ttl-and-health-check).

step.name: write-promotion-and-fencing
step.input: Database vendor documentation for promotion; the app's connection configuration.
step.action: Write `database.promotion_procedure` (runbook reference and command), `fencing` (how the old primary stops accepting writes before promotion) and `single_writer_enforcement` (how only one writer endpoint can exist).
step.output: Promotion, fencing and single-writer text in `database`.
step.decision-gate: No fencing step means split brain on the first real failover (fm-03).

step.name: write-failback
step.input: The promotion procedure; the replication topology after failover.
step.action: Fill `failback.trigger`, its own `rpo_minutes` / `rto_minutes`, the `reconciliation_step` for writes accepted in the secondary, and the `procedure` back to the primary or to two healthy regions.

step.name: run-live-drill
step.input: `drill.checklist[]` (at least five steps: freeze, fence, promote, flip DNS, scale, synthetic transaction, record manual steps); a bounded traffic slice; a drill window.
step.action: Run the drill on real traffic; fill `drill.last` with `date`, `scope_services[]`, `traffic_percent`, `measured_rto_minutes`, `measured_rpo_minutes`, `manual_steps[]`; write `dns.observed_propagation_seconds` from the timer; set `drill.mechanics_last_changed_at` to the last change to replication, DNS or promotion.
step.decision-gate: The drill is re-run after any change to replication, DNS or promotion mechanics (r-drill-live-with-measured-results).

step.name: decide-and-label
step.action: Write `decision` naming the chosen pattern once with achievable versus required numbers; add `unverified` if `drill.last` is null or older than `mechanics_last_changed_at`. Add `evidence[]` (drill report, replication dashboard, quota request, backfill job); set `review.cadence` and `next_review_at`. Fill `templates/skeleton.md.j2`; run `scripts/validate-multi-region-failover-pattern-pack.py --file`; the named owner reviews before commit.
step.decision-gate: A pack labelled `unverified` schedules its drill before `next_review_at` (r-drill-live-with-measured-results, 03 human checkpoint).

list.item: Pack validates via `scripts/validate-multi-region-failover-pattern-pack.py`, including achievable-versus-required and lag-versus-RPO checks.
`drill.last` is dated after `mechanics_last_changed_at`, or `decision` carries `unverified` and a drill is scheduled.
Every dependency on the failover path is reachable from the secondary or has a drilled bypass.
